verifications.verifierNote: Read both files in full. The duplication is real (toastStore.ts:10 `const listeners = new Set<() => void>()`, :12-14 `emit()`, :39-44 `subscribeToToasts`; apiKey.ts:3 `listeners`, :5-7 `notify()`, :30-35 `subscribeToApiKey`) but it is not a type-safety defect and does not meet the spec's definition of `generic-opportunity` ('duplicated TYPE DEFINITIONS across modules that could collapse to a single generic'). Zero type definitions are duplicated: the only shared type is the builtin `() => void`, and toastStore's sole declared type (`ToastMessage`, :3-7) has no counterpart in apiKey.ts. The proposed `createStore<T>` has no `T` to bind on the apiKey side, because apiKey.ts holds no snapshot state at all - `getApiKey()` (:9-12) reads `localStorage` on every call, so there is nothing for `useSyncExternalStore` to snapshot except a derived value. What actually overlaps is a listener Set plus a 1-line for-loop, ~6 lines total across 2 modules; extracting a generic store for that is the speculative abstraction the project's own rules forbid. The finding's own text concedes 'the types are correct in both... this is a duplication finding, not a soundness one'.
verifications.reachability: n/a - no unsound value can flow through either module; both are fully type-correct and there is no assertion, `any`, or suppression at either site.
verifications.blastRadius: 2 modules, ~6 duplicated implementation lines, 0 duplicated type declarations, 2 React consumers.

verifications.verifierNote: Pattern present verbatim at useFocusTrap.ts:25 - `const restoreTo = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;`. `document.activeElement` is typed `Element | null` in lib.dom.d.ts and `Element` declares no `focus()`; the assertion is the only reason `restoreTo?.focus()` at :29 compiles, and `?.` guards nullness, not method existence. Severity `low` is right and honestly argued: every realistic `activeElement` (including `document.body`) is an `HTMLElement` or `SVGElement`, both of which do declare `focus()`, so no crash is reachable today. It is a genuine `as T` over a base type where a narrow is available, which is exactly the category. Not generated code; the file is hand-written and carries a doc comment (:7-12).
verifications.reachability: Cleanup path of the effect at :22-31, which runs on every modal close (Dialog, ConfirmDialog, chat drawer, quiz). Reached constantly; the assertion just never turns out to be wrong.

verifications.suggestedPatch: useFocusTrap.ts:25 -> `const restoreTo = document.activeElement;` (drop the cast) and :29 -> `if (restoreTo instanceof HTMLElement || restoreTo instanceof SVGElement) restoreTo.focus();`. Risk: `instanceof` is false across realms, so an element focused in another document would no longer be restored - not a case this app can produce.

verifications.verifierNote: Both assertions are present (useFocusTrap.ts:47 `const first = items[0]!;`, :48 `const last = items[items.length - 1]!;`) but they are correct as written and the proposed fix does not improve them. Line 45 (`if (items.length === 0) return;`) proves both accesses in-range, which the established baseline already records. Under the current tsconfig (`strict: true`, no `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`) they are no-ops; under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` they would become load-bearing and STILL correct - and TypeScript has no control-flow analysis that can narrow `items[items.length - 1]`, so the suggested alternatives do not remove the assertion: `items.at(-1)` returns `HTMLElement | undefined` and `const [first] = items` is likewise `HTMLElement | undefined`. The 'inconsistent with line 26' argument does not hold either: `focusable()[0]?.focus()` at :26 sits in a scope with no length guard and makes a single optional call, so `?.` is the right idiom there and `!` is the right idiom here. A guarded, provably-true non-null assertion is not what the `non-null-assertion` category targets ('crashes at runtime if the assumption is wrong' - this assumption cannot be wrong).

Repo-wide grep confirms `dateRead` appears only in goodreads.ts (:9, :90, :105, :113) and goodreads.test.ts:22 - `importGoodreadsRows` (useLibrary.tsx:150-160) maps title/author/category/status/rating/coverImageUrl/hasPdf and never reads it - and `finishedAt` appears ONLY at its declaration, types.ts:40, with zero readers and zero writers in src/. PROBLEM 2 (the `new Date('2023/05/14')` hazard) is explicitly contingent on future code the finding itself confirms does not exist - it should be recorded as a note attached to any future wiring-up, not as a present-tense boundary finding. The defect is therefore a type-honesty one of the dead-declaration kind: the exported parse result advertises data the pipeline discards, so a consumer reasonably concludes read-dates survive an import. verifications.verifierNote: The pattern is present (types.ts:64 `model: string`, with the doc comment at :63 naming 'legacy' as the migration sentinel) but the recommended narrowing would introduce the very defect this audit exists to find, so this should not be actioned. `Summary.model` is a PERSISTED HISTORICAL PROVENANCE field: it records which model produced a stored summary, and models.ts's own comment says 'A Google rename is a one-line change here'. The moment that rename happens, every already-persisted summary in IndexedDB still carries the OLD id - which would no longer be a member of `(typeof MODELS)[keyof typeof MODELS] | 'legacy'`. Narrowing the field therefore makes the declared type false about the data on the read path, i.e. a lying type, which is strictly worse than the current honest `string`. The branded-type bar is also not met: I grepped every write (chat.ts:14, quiz.ts:11, recommend.ts:25, summarize.ts:39/47/63/89, tts.ts:19 all pass `MODELS.*` to the SDK, not to this field; the only writes to `Summary.model` are summarize.ts's own value, migrate.ts:131 `'legacy'`, and three test fixtures) and there is no read anywhere in src/ - so there is no call site where a wrong value could arrive and be consumed, and no adjacent same-typed parameter to swap it with. The project invariant 'model IDs live only in src/lib/ai/models.ts' is about where IDs are AUTHORED, which migrate.ts:131 does not violate ('legacy' is not a model id).

verifications.verifierNote: Lines confirmed: AudioPlayer.tsx:62-66 `handleLoadedMetadata` -> `setDuration(audioRef.current.duration)`, :212 `max={duration || 100}`, :217 `{formatTime(duration)}` with `formatTime` at :97-101 (`Math.floor(time / 60)` / `Math.floor(time % 60)`), and `duration` initialised `0` at :21. Second, reachability is nil today, as the finding itself says: the only producer is `setActiveAudioTrack` (AppShell.tsx:82) fed by locally generated WAV blobs whose headers carry a finite duration. The related weakness is that `duration` enters state unguarded at :64 from `HTMLMediaElement.duration`, which is `NaN` when unknown and `Infinity` for stream-like media, so `formatTime(duration)` at :217 would render the literal 'Infinity:NaN' or 'NaN:NaN'.
